title: Policy rationale tagging and latency-correlated audit ledger
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Background: Smart routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants) are currently logged as basic decision events but lack structured rationale and a joinable latency signal. This makes it hard to answer: why did a request route to region X, why a fallback model was chosen, and which routing rule version made the decision when latency or quality regressions occur.

Goal: Implement a compact, queryable audit ledger that attaches policy rationale tags to routing decisions and correlates them with per-hop latency metrics. The ledger should be cheap to emit in the hot path, retain enough provenance to debug incidents and drive post-hoc analytics, and respect privacy/compliance constraints.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every routing decision emitted from the router includes a standardized "rationale" tuple: {policy_id, policy_version, decision_reason, evaluated_inputs} encoded compactly (see schema below).
- Per-hop latency buckets (p50/p95/p99) and exact elapsed micros for sampled decisions are linked to the same ledger entry ID so traces and audit logs can be joined.
- Deterministic sampling for full payload snapshots: 0.1% global + client-tier override for enterprise customers.
- Hot-path overhead <= 3% tail latency cost measured on bench harness (synthetic traffic) with continuous batching enabled.
- Hot telemetry written to a compact Kafka compacted topic; full snapshots archived to encrypted S3 for 90 days.
- PII redaction rules applied: client IP, full prompt text removed in ledger; a hashed prompt-prefix fingerprint is allowed.

Proposed ledger schema (textual):
- ledger_id: uuidv4 string
- ts_utc: iso8601
- request_key: deterministic string (customer_id|route|request_hash)
comments: 2025-02-10 - Priya Singh: Created ticket after post-mortem for 2025-02-09 spike where fallback model churned and we couldn't attribute why decisions diverged.

2025-02-14 - Daniel Meyer: Spike implemented a minimal prototype writing a compact base64-encoded rationale blob to a local log. Observed ~1.8% p99 increase in microbenchmark. Shared draft in #infra-observability. GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-observability/pull/102
2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel (PM): Design review notes - require enterprise-exempt sampling toggle and GDPR retention settings. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-21 - Design sync: Agreed to use protobuf v3 for hot-path encoding to minimize size; fallback JSON for archives. Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/RI/Policy+Rationale+Ledger

2025-02-25 - Daniel Meyer: Prototype switched to a compact protobuf and added deterministic sampling key (customer_id + route). Payload size dropped from ~1.2KB to ~240B average. Bench harness shows overhead down to ~1.4% p99. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-observability/pull/118
2025-02-28 - Security review (Liam O'Connor): Flagged needing KMS-wrapped encryption for archived snapshots and additional PII checks. Filed follow-up: ENG-87902

2025-03-01 - Priya Singh: Decided on storage plan: Kafka compacted topic for ledger (7d hot retention + compacted keys), S3 cold snapshots (encrypted, 90d). Dashboard prototype in Grafana references ledger_id as join key.

2025-03-04 - Daniel Meyer: Implemented join key in request context and added per-hop elapsed micros. End-to-end integration test added. Observability team to validate dashboards next week. Pending: performance review in large-scale cluster and rollout plan for canary group.
